content.title: About
content.content: Applesauce cookie is a soft biscuit made from whole‑grain flour, sugar, butter, and natural applesauce. It has a gentle sweet flavor with a hint of apple tartness, suitable as a snack or dessert.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Applesauce retains some vitamin C and fiber found in fresh apples.
Adding fruit puree to biscuits became popular in Europe in the 19th century as a way to increase moisture and shelf life.
Applesauce cookies are often used in children's meals because of their soft texture and moderate sweetness.
The combination of whole‑grain flour and applesauce makes the product more nutritious than standard sugary cookies.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Applesauce and whole‑grain flour provide dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: A small amount of vitamin C from the applesauce helps support the immune system.

items.title: Low in trans fats
items.content: When made with non‑hydrogenated butter, the cookie contains no trans fats.

items.title: Moderate sugar level
items.content: Added sugar is balanced with the natural sweetness of applesauce, lowering the overall glycemic impact.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Phenolic compounds from apples provide antioxidant benefits.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: The cookie contains gluten and is not suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although some sugar is replaced by applesauce, the product still contains added sugar and should be limited for diabetics.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some commercial versions may include preservatives; check the label if you avoid them.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Applesauce cookies can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, added to yogurt, used in baby food, or as a base for dessert tarts. For extra aroma, warm them briefly before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cookies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer storage (over 2 weeks) keep them refrigerated to maintain freshness and prevent drying out.
